Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Create ONE new script + test. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no model calls, no sends. The script SHELLS OUT to ssh at runtime, but TESTS MUST NEVER touch the network: the remote-command runner is an injected callable and every test passes a fake.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production code with no tests, fewer than 6 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these — both new):
  scripts/vps_schedule_snapshot.py
  tests/test_vps_schedule_snapshot.py

WHY THIS EXISTS, measured today. scripts/heijunka_board.py renders the next six Thursday slots but
currently exits 1 ("unverified") and stamps every slot "local-unverified", because local episode state
is NOT the publisher. Episodes/ is gitignored and the deploy script syncs code only, so the laptop and
the production host hold different truths: on 2026-07-31 the laptop reported "8 in flight, healthy"
while the production host had ZERO episodes scheduled to publish, and four episodes that WERE live in
production still showed as unpublished locally. Until the board can read production, it can only say
"I cannot tell you". This script is what lets it say something true.

READ FIRST: scripts/heijunka_board.py — specifically how it consumes `--vps-schedule PATH` and the exact
shape it expects for each entry (episode_id, publish_date, and whatever else build_board reads). Match
that contract EXACTLY; the board is already merged and must not be edited by this lane.
Also read scripts/deploy-podcast-vps.sh for the established ssh invocation style (host, user, PEM path
resolution via a PEM_FILE env default, StrictHostKeyChecking flag). Reuse that style; do not invent a
new connection convention and do not hardcode a private key path that only exists on one machine —
resolve it from an env var with the documented default.

BUILD scripts/vps_schedule_snapshot.py:
  REMOTE_EPISODE_PROBE — a single, self-contained python -c program (as a string constant) that runs ON
  the remote host inside its checkout and prints ONE json document to stdout: every episode directory
  with its episode_id (the directory name), stage, publish_date, episode_type, and whether it already
  has publish evidence (a transistor/youtube publish_status). It must be read-only, must not import
  anything outside the standard library plus the repo's own json files (walk episodes/*/episode.json
  directly — do NOT import the repo's modules, so a broken deploy cannot make the probe fail), and must
  tolerate an unreadable episode.json by emitting that episode with stage "unreadable" rather than
  dying.

  fetch_snapshot(*, runner, now) -> dict
      Calls runner(command) -> CompletedProcess-like (returncode, stdout, stderr) and returns
      {"schema": "vps-schedule-v1", "fetched_at": iso from now, "host": <host>,
       "episodes": [...], "schedule": [{"episode_id","publish_date"} ...], "problems": [...]}
      "schedule" contains ONLY future-publishable episodes: a publish_date present, not already
      published, and stage not terminal/killed — that is what the board consumes as slot claims.
      A nonzero returncode, empty stdout, or unparseable JSON returns a snapshot with an EMPTY schedule
      and a recorded problem — and NEVER raises. Critical semantic: a failed fetch must be
      distinguishable from a genuinely empty production schedule, because the board alarms on the
      latter. Include an explicit "ok": bool so the caller cannot confuse the two.

  main(): --output PATH (default state/receipts/vps-schedule.json), --host, --user, --remote-dir,
      --timeout. Writes the snapshot atomically (temp file + rename) so a partial write can never be
      read as truth. Exit 0 when ok, 2 when the fetch failed (so cron alarms on a broken snapshot —
      a stale snapshot silently reused would recreate the exact deception this fixes). Print a one-line
      human summary: host, episode count, schedule count, ok/failed.

  STALENESS: fetch_snapshot stamps fetched_at; also provide snapshot_is_stale(snapshot, *, now,
      max_age_hours=26) -> bool so the board/cron can refuse a snapshot older than a day. Unparseable
      fetched_at is STALE (fail closed).

TESTS (tests/test_vps_schedule_snapshot.py; at least 6; fake runner ONLY, no network, fixed now):
 (1) THE REAL CASE: a fake runner returning a realistic probe payload (mixed stages, one already
     published, one future solo, one guest with a publish_date) yields a schedule containing only the
     future-publishable ones, and ok is True;
 (2) NEGATIVE: runner returns returncode 1 -> ok False, empty schedule, problem recorded, main exits 2,
     and NOTHING is written over an existing good snapshot... verify the atomic-write behaviour by
     asserting the pre-existing file is either untouched or fully replaced, never truncated;
 (3) NEGATIVE: runner returns garbage stdout -> ok False with a parse problem, no exception;
 (4) NEGATIVE: a failed fetch is distinguishable from a real empty schedule (assert two snapshots with
     the same empty schedule differ in ok / problems — the board must not read a broken fetch as
     "production has nothing scheduled");
 (5) an already-published episode never appears in schedule;
 (6) snapshot_is_stale: fresh -> False, 30h old -> True, unparseable fetched_at -> True;
 (7) the emitted schedule is accepted by the board: feed it to heijunka_board.build_board and assert the
     slots come back sourced from the snapshot rather than local-unverified (prove the contract end to
     end; import the board module, do not copy its logic);
 (8) determinism: same payload + same now -> identical snapshot document.
